public.in_one_sentence: Attacks on, or the closing or reopening of, Gulf shipping that change what Sri Lanka pays for fuel, or whether cargo arrives.
tell_me_if: Ships are attacked, sunk or stopped in or near the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman
Brent or Dubai crude moves more than 5% in a day on Gulf news
A ceasefire, deal or naval escort scheme reopens Hormuz, or the blockade of Iranian ports changes
Colombo or other South Asian ports report diverted, delayed or stranded cargo from the Gulf
War-risk insurance for Gulf voyages is withdrawn or its price jumps
ignore: Analyst forecasts of oil prices with no new event
Nuclear-talks headlines with no effect on shipping

match.headline: Container ship sinks near Strait of Hormuz after projectile strike
Brent jumps 5% as Iran steps up attacks on Hormuz tankers
Navies agree escort scheme to reopen Strait of Hormuz

not_match: Iran and US negotiators meet again with no announcement
Oil analysts raise year-end price forecast

exposure.how_it_reaches_us: Crude passes Hormuz; a stop raises the import bill.
Fuel and goods letters of credit grow or stall.
Importers face higher costs and delays.

serious: Colombo-bound fuel cargoes stopped or diverted
Sri Lanka announces fuel rationing or an emergency purchase
private.notes: Hormuz transits fell to a fraction of normal after attacks since March 2026. Treasury cares about the dollar bill and the rupee; trade finance about delays on import LCs.
